decoy_bugs.summary: When BloomTokenLog turns over its filters at periods_forward == 2, it throws away the tokens recorded in filter_2 instead of moving them into filter_1, so a retry or NEW_TOKEN token used in the previous period can be redeemed a second time.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: A token that check_and_insert has already accepted (its expiry falls in the second period) is accepted again with Ok(()) after another token whose expiry falls two periods past period_1_start has triggered the turnover branch.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: BloomTokenLog::check_and_insert (quinn-proto/src/bloom_token_log.rs:89-93) is called with a token whose expiry falls two lifetimes past period_1_start, which runs the periods_forward == 2 arm that resets the filters and advances period_1_start by lifetime.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran a test in a copy under tmp/probe through ./run (cargo test -p quinn-proto --lib probe_tests::probe_bloom_turnover) using BloomTokenLog::default() and lifetime 10s. Nonce 1 at t, nonce 2 at t+L and nonce 3 at t+2L (the turnover) were all accepted. Replaying nonce 2 at t+L and nonce 3 at t+2L both returned Err (printed 'B replay false', 'C replay false'). The code at lines 91-93 does `state.filter_1 = take(&mut state.filter_2)`, which moves the entries over rather than dropping them.

decoy_bugs.summary: When TokenMemoryCache is full, adding a token for a new server name frees the least-recently-used slab slot and reuses it. The deferred lookup.remove then deletes the new server's mapping, so the token just stored can never be taken.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: With lru.len() >= max_server_names, storing a token for a server name not yet in the cache leaves that name missing from lookup, and the next take() for it returns None.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: State::store (quinn-proto/src/token_memory_cache.rs:96-110) handles a vacant lookup entry while the cache is full: lru.remove(lru.lru()) frees a slot, lru.insert reuses it, and lookup.remove(&removed_slot) runs after hmap_entry.insert.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran probe_tests::probe_token_cache_lru_and_eviction through ./run on a copy of the crate. With TokenMemoryCache::new(1, 2) I inserted x, y and z in turn, then take() returned x=None, y=None, z=Some("z1"): the newest server stays reachable and only the evicted one is gone. Reading the code agrees: removed_key holds the evicted entry's server_name (an Arc<str>), not a slot index. That name cannot equal the new name, because the new name came in through a Vacant entry.

false_findings.text:
**Token log forgets used tokens on bloom conversion**
quinn-proto/src/bloom_token_log.rs:173 (Filter::check_and_insert).
When the per-period HashSet grows past filter_max_bytes and is turned into a bloom filter, the fingerprints stored so far are lost. Every token redeemed before the conversion can then be replayed and is accepted as fresh.
The new BloomFilter is built and assigned with `*self = Self::Bloom(bloom)` after iterating `&*hset`, but the loop inserts `item` (a `&u64` reference) through FxBuildHasher's reference hashing, so the bits it sets do not match those later checked by `bloom.insert(&fingerprint)`.
With BloomTokenLog::new(256, 4), inserting 200 distinct nonces and then replaying all 200 accepted 187 of the replays.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran probe_tests::probe_bloom_conversion through ./run (cargo test -p quinn-proto --lib, copy under tmp/probe) with BloomTokenLog::new(256, 4), 200 distinct nonces in one period, then the same 200 again. It printed 'replays accepted: 0', so every replay was rejected after the set had converted. The conversion did happen: the first false positive on a fresh nonce came at insert 129, which a plain HashSet cannot produce. Both paths call bloom.insert with a &u64, so they hash the same way.

false_findings.text:
**ACK range iterator underflows when a range ends at packet 0**
quinn-proto/src/frame.rs:822 (AckIter::next).
An ACK frame whose last additional range reaches packet number 0 makes the receiver panic with 'attempt to subtract with overflow' while processing the ACK, so a remote peer can crash a debug-built endpoint or wrap packet numbers in release.
AckIter::next subtracts `block + gap + 2` from `self.largest` before it knows whether another range follows, and scan_ack_blocks validates only that each range's lower bound is non-negative, not this look-ahead subtraction.
Decoding the frame bytes `02 0a 00 01 03 04 01` (largest 10, first block 3, gap 4, block 1) with frame::Iter and collecting ack.iter() panicked at frame.rs:822.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran probe_tests::probe_ack_iter_reaches_zero through ./run in both debug and release. That exact frame decoded to ranges [7..=10, 0..=1] with no panic. So did [5..=5, 0..=0], a lone [0..=0], and a frame with largest 2^62-1 whose second range is [0..=0]. A frame whose gap goes below 0 was rejected as malformed (err=true). Reading the code: the subtraction at line 822 runs only when a gap varint follows, and scan_ack_blocks has already checked smallest - (gap+2) - block >= 0 for that gap.

false_findings.text:
**Maximum-length connection IDs rejected as malformed**
quinn-proto/src/frame.rs:662 (Iter::try_next).
A NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame carrying a 20-byte connection ID, which RFC 9000 allows, is rejected with FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR "malformed" and the connection is closed. Peers whose CID generator uses the full length cannot migrate or rotate CIDs.
The length check rejects lengths at the MAX_CID_SIZE boundary instead of only lengths beyond it, so 20 is refused along with 21 and up.
Feeding frame::Iter the bytes 18 03 01 14 followed by 20 CID bytes and 16 reset-token bytes returned Err(InvalidFrame { reason: "malformed" }).
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Read frame.rs:662: the check is `length > MAX_CID_SIZE || length == 0`, and MAX_CID_SIZE is 20 (lib.rs:329), so 20 is allowed. I also ran probe_tests::probe_new_cid_len_20 through ./run with those exact bytes. It printed 'NEW_CID ok len=20 seq=3', meaning the frame decoded to Frame::NewConnectionId with a 20-byte id.

false_findings.text:
**Unchecked VarInt built from locally opened stream IDs**
quinn-proto/src/lib.rs:280 (From<StreamId> for VarInt).
If a peer advertises a stream limit near 2^62, Streams::open can hand out stream indices at or above 2^60, whose IDs are 2^62 or more. Turning such an ID into a VarInt breaks the type's < 2^62 invariant, and VarInt::size or encode then panics with "malformed VarInt" when a STREAM frame header is written.
The conversion calls the unsafe VarInt::from_u64_unchecked on the raw StreamId, while Streams::open (connection/streams/mod.rs:57) builds the ID as `index << 2 | dir | side` with no upper bound beyond state.max.
The safety precondition of from_u64_unchecked (x < 2^62) is never established on this path: no assertion or bound exists between StreamId::new and lib.rs:280.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Read the paths that set state.max. StreamsState::received_max_streams (streams/state.rs:711) rejects counts above MAX_STREAM_COUNT = 1<<60, the MAX_STREAMS frame handler (connection/mod.rs:2849) does the same, and transport_parameters.rs:511-512 bounds the initial_max_streams values. So Streams::open's index stays below 2^60 and the ID below 2^62. Ran probe_tests::probe_stream_id_bound through ./run: StreamId::new(Server, Uni, MAX_STREAM_COUNT-1) converted to VarInt 4611686018427387903 (= 2^62-1), which is < 2^62, with size() = 8 and no panic.

false_findings.text:
**Per-server token queue in TokenMemoryCache grows without bound**
quinn-proto/src/token_memory_cache.rs:88 (State::store).
A server that keeps sending NEW_TOKEN frames to the same server name makes the client's per-server VecDeque grow by one entry per token in release builds, ignoring max_tokens_per_server, so a malicious server can make the client's memory grow without bound.
The only thing enforcing the cap on the occupied-entry path is the `debug_assert!(tokens.len() == self.max_tokens_per_server)`, which release builds compile out, and the pop_front sits under that same branch.
A release-mode test inserting 10,000 tokens for one name into TokenMemoryCache::new(4, 3) and then draining it with take() returned all 10,000 tokens.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran probe_tests::probe_token_queue_bound through ./run with `cargo test --release`. After 10,000 inserts for "srv" into TokenMemoryCache::new(4, 3), draining it printed 'retained 3 tokens [9997, 9998, 9999]'. Reading lines 88-92: `if tokens.len() >= self.max_tokens_per_server { ... tokens.pop_front().unwrap(); }` is ordinary control flow that runs in release. Only the debug_assert inside it is compiled out.
